content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Great — let's start by getting clear on what you really want out of this, before anything gets built.

A quick note on how I'll work with you: we'll go step by step. First I want to understand your goal, then I'll show you working screens to react to — you won't need to organize anything or think in technical terms. I'll handle all of that.

So, starting with the "why":

**When this bookmark app is finished and working well, what would be different from how you handle bookmarks today?** For example — is the pain right now that bookmarks get lost or messy somewhere, that you can't find them again later, that they're scattered across different places, or something else entirely?

And a second thing I'm curious about: when you say "save and manage" — is the heart of this mainly about **collecting** links quickly, or more about **finding them again** later when you need them? Knowing which side matters more will shape everything that follows.

Take it in your own words — there's no wrong answer here.

Right now my bookmarks become a pile that I rarely revisit because I can’t quickly find the one I remember saving. I’d like one dependable place where I can save a link quickly, give it useful tags or a note, and later find it by searching whatever I remember about it.

Finding things again is the bigger priority, though saving should still feel effortless. I’d also like to separate things I intend to read later from things I’ve finished with, without having to delete useful links.

content:
That covers the boundary and error situations across saving, finding, and the read-later views. I think we've reached a complete, coherent picture for a first version.

Here's everything that's settled so far — in plain terms:

**Saving a link**
- Paste an address and the title, description, site icon, and preview image fill in automatically; you can edit the title/description before saving.
- Only the link is required; you can add tags (with suggestions from tags you've used before) and a private note.
- If a link can't be read, you can still save it and fill in the details yourself; if it isn't a real web address, you're asked to fix it.
- Saving the same link twice never makes a duplicate — you're taken to the existing one to update it (including when you edit a link to match another).

**Finding a link again**
- One search box looks across title, description, note, tags, and address at once, live as you type, ignoring capitalization, with matches highlighted and a match count.
- Powerful searches: exact tag with `#tag`, combining words, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` with parentheses, and `"exact phrases"`.
- Click any tag to filter by it; note-only matches show a highlighted excerpt so you know why they appeared.

**Read later vs. finished**
- Choose "save to read later" (on by default) or save as a reference.
- All / To read / Finished tabs with counts; mark items finished or move them back — nothing is ever deleted, and finished items stay searchable.

**When things aren't tidy**
- Friendly messages for empty lists and no-results; long content wraps neatly.

A couple of things we agreed to leave for **later versions** (I've noted them): automatic dead-link detection, and general look-and-feel polish.

**May I now move on to building this as the real application?** Once you approve, I'll switch from exploring to implementing this scope.

Not quite yet. The saving, search, and reading flows are well captured, but “manage bookmarks” still needs a few important areas settled before building:

- I need to delete a bookmark permanently, and separately archive one so it disappears from the normal list and ordinary searches but can be restored from an Archive view.
- I need to select several bookmarks and add or remove tags, mark read or unread, archive, or delete them together. I’d also like the option to apply an action to every result in the current search or view—not bookmarks outside that filter.
